 : JUDGMENT :
The petitioner has filed this petition being aggrieved by the arbitral award passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru, in No. LAQ / ARB / NH-7 /
CR / 73/140/33/31/30/29/28/2011-12 dated 01.10.2019 in respect of Sy. No.64/1 measuring 4949.6 Sq. feet of A.P. No.192/2021 Kadenahalli village, Jala Hobli, Bengaluru North Addl. Taluka,
Bengaluru Urban District.

 National Highways Authority of India
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text:
.2. The definite case of the petitioner is that the property bearing Sy. No.64/1 measuring 4949.6 Sq.
feet of Kadenahalli village, Jala Hobli, Bengaluru North Addl. Taluka, Bengaluru Urban District has been acquired under Preliminary Notification dated 09.12.2009 and Final Notification dated 02.07.2010.
Subsequently the respondent No.2/LAO has awarded a total compensation of Rs.65,03,774/- in respect of petitioner's land and Rs. 3,43,905/- towards compound, gate and well on the aforesaid land.
The petitioner received the same under protest and filed an application on 17.10.2011 for enhancing the compensation at the rate of Rs.5,000/- per Sq. feet.
Accordingly, the said application taken by the respondent No.2 for consideration.

.3. In the said petition, the respondent No.2 filed statement of objection stating that the contention urged by the petitioner are baseless and the same are made A.P. No.192/2021 without any substance.
The petitioner has not produced any relevant documents to justify their claim for enhanced compensation and the claim of the petitioners cannot be sustained in law.

Hence,
question of enhancement of compensation will not arise and the claim of the petitioner is liable to be dismissed by the respondent No.2.
Accordingly, prayed to dismiss the reference.

.4. Thereafter, the Arbitrator hold an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR-73 / 140 / 33 / 31 / 30 / 29 / 28 2011-12 dated 01.10.2019.
.5.

Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting up the following :
Ashadevi K R Since Dead By Her Lr ... vs The Special Deputy Commissioner And ... on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24427893/
2 :GROUNDS:

entities.text: Ashadevi K R Since Dead By Her Lr
entities.label: PETITIONER

sentences.text:
The petitioner claims that the respondent No.3 fixed the amount of Rs. 200 lakhs per acre for agricultural land and Rs.1314/- per Square feet towards sites of A.P.
No.192/2021 BDA and BMRDA, is unjust and against to the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Further the respondent No.1 has not adopted the yardstick applied to the other cases.

Further the award passed by the  respondent No.3 and also the enhancement made by the respondent No.1 by fixing Rs.1,500/- per Sq. feet is against to the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and the compensation so awarded cannot be termed as fair compensation and among other grounds, prayed to call for the records of the arbitral proceedings No. LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR-1/2018-19 from respondent No.1 and also to set aside the award passed by the respondent No.1.
.6.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The respondent No.3 filed detailed objections claiming that the application is not maintainable either in law or on facts and the same is liable to be dismissed A.P.
No.192/2021 in limine.
Further, at the outset that the petitioner has no locus-standi to file the top noted petition since they were not parties to the arbitration proceedings before the respondent No.1.

The claimant before the respondent No.1 i.e., K.R.
Ashadevi had expired on 10.05.2012 itself i.e., during pendency of the arbitration proceedings.
Subsequently no efforts were made to bring the LRs of the deceased claimant on record before the respondent No.1, so petitioner has no right to challenge the arbitral award dated 01.10.2019.
Further, the respondent No. 3 passed the award as per the guidance value produced before the Arbitrator pertaining to the year 2011.
The petitioner is attempting to mislead this Court by drawing reference to incorrect/wholly inapplicable guidance notification.
The respondent No.1 totally denied all the grounds claimed by the petitioner in the petition.

The Arbitrator/ respondent No. 3 passed the award after giving full opportunity of hearing to the petitioner by considering the material evidence on record for A.P. No.192/2021 enhancement of compensation together with all other statutory benefits available under the LA Act in accordance with law and prayed for dismissal of the petition.

.7. The respondents No.1 to 3 though served with the notice, the respondent No.1 appeared before the Court through DGP, respondent No.3 appeared before the Court through his advocate and respondent No.2 remained absent.

The entire records in LAQ/ARB/NH- 7/CR-73 / 140 / 33 / 31 /
30 / 29 / 28 2011-12 dated 01.10.2019 secured from the Arbitrator.

.8. On the basis of above, the point for consideration is that:
Ashadevi K R Since Dead By Her Lr ... vs The Special Deputy Commissioner And ... on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24427893/
3
" Whether
the impugned award of the Arbitrator/SLAO is against law, fact, evidence and probabilities of the case and liable to be intervened by this Court?"
.9. Heard the arguments.
Perused the materials on record, on that basis my finding on the above point is in the negative, for the following:
A.P. No.192/2021 REASONS .10.
POINT:
Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note an admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

The petitioner K.R.
Ashadevi is an owner of the property bearing Sy. No.64/1 measuring 4949.6 Sq. feet of Kadenahalli village, Jala Hobli, Bengaluru North Additional Taluka and the said property has been acquired for widening of NH-7 under Preliminary Notification dated 09.12.2009 and Final Notification dated 02.07.2010,
is an admitted fact.

It is also an admitted and undisputed fact in this case that the respondent No.2/Special Land Acquisition and Competent Authority of National Highways Authority of India being a SLAO determined the compensation at Rs. 1,314/- per Sq. feet for the acquired land.

entities.text: Special Land Acquisition and Competent Authority of National Highways Authority of India
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: It is also admitted and undisputed fact that a sum of Rs.65,03,774/-
being the land value
and Rs. 3,43,905/- towards compound, gate and well on the aforesaid acquired property
, was disbursed to the petitioner as compensation.

Subsequent to the receipt of compensation or passing of the award, the petitioner Smt. K.R. Ashadevi filed an application on 17.10.2011 before the respondent No.3 claiming that she is entitled for compensation at the rate of Rs.5,000/- per Sq. feet.
On basis of the said application, the respondent No.3 hold an i n q u i r y a n d p a s s e d c o m m o n o r d e r i n L A Q / A R B / N H - 7/CR-73/140/33/31/30/29/28/2011-12 dated 01.10.2019.
The respondent No.3 in its order enhanced the compensation at Rs.1,500/- per Square feet from Rs. 1,314/- per Square feet and awarded additional compensation of Rs.186/- per Square feet.
.12. After the death of petitioner K.R. Ashadevi, her LRs were brought on record as petitioners 1 and 2.
The petitioners challenging the award of the Arbitrator / respondent No. 1 claiming that the respondent No.1 has not properly enhanced the compensation prevailing to the market value.

Further claim of the petitioner is that in some other cases, the respondent No.1 / Arbitrator has enhanced the compensation, which is A.P. No.192/2021 much higher than the compensation awarded to the petitioners.

If it were so, it is for the petitioners to prove the said fact by placing particulars of the such cases in which the Arbitrator has enhanced the compensation which is much higher than the compensation awarded to the petitioners.

Further the petitioners have not produced any material on record to show that the market value of the acquired property when the preliminary notification has been issued was more than Rs.5,000 per Sq. feet or it is / was Rs. 4,000/- per Sq.
feet as claimed by the petitioners.
In the absence of such material before the court certainly this court cannot find fault with the order of the Arbitrator.

Infact the petitioners have not at all produced even scrap of paper to show that the compensation awarded by the Arbitrator is contrary to the compensation awarded to the others to the property acquired under the same notification,
same village or adjacent property of the petitioners.

Absolutely there is no material placed by the petitioners before the court to show that the award A.P. No.192/2021 passed by the respondent No.
Ashadevi K R Since Dead By Her Lr ... vs The Special Deputy Commissioner And ... on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24427893/
4 2 / Arbitrator is perverse or against any law that needs to be interfered by this court.

Accordingly,
the point No. 1 is held in the negative.

In the result, proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act,
1996 by the petitioners is hereby dismissed.

Consequently, the award passed by the respondent No.1 in case No. LAQ / ARB /
NH-7 / CR / 73 / 140 / 33 / 31/30 /29/28/2011-12 dated 01.10.2019 in respect of Sy.
No.64/1 measuring 4949.6 Sq. feet of Kadenahalli village, Jala Hobli, Bengaluru North Addl. Taluka, Bengaluru Urban District
is hereby confirmed.
Parties to bear their own cost.
Office is directed to send back the Lower Court Records.
(Dictated to the Stenographer Grade-I, transcribed by her, revised by me and after corrections, pronounced in open Court on this the 7th day of February, 2025)
(PADMA PRASAD) II Addl. City Civil and Sessions Judge, & Spl. Judge, Bangalore.
